doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dillard University and a Columbia Records digression
title: From Dallas to Dillard University in 1951 with Ellis Marsalis
summary: After a mid-term high school graduation his parents shipped him to Dillard in New Orleans, where he enrolled the same day as Ellis Marsalis for about half a semester.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Okay, let's move from Dallas to Denver.
So, tell us about how you ended up at University of Denver.
Well, uh, my parents and I, uh, uh, were on summer vacation in between my graduation of high school and college, you know, in that period. So uh …
Was it a given that you were going to university?

No! No. I had already uh, uh, been to Dillard University in New Orleans for a half a semester. I graduated high school on a Friday and my folks shipped me out that Monday to New Orleans. They didn't want me to hang around 'til the school year started, 'cause I was a mid-term graduate. So uh …
Were you a good student, by the way?

Uh …Uh … [laughs] sometimes. As much as I could be, yes. Yeah, I uh, I uh, I did okay in, especially in high school. In college I started to get more attracted to playing in uh … sort of like, uh, uh, made me deviate from my intended uh, uh, uh, uh target, uh, goal, uh, was to get a college education.
So, I didn't know about the New Orleans episode, so …

It was sorta short. Me and Ellis Marsalis enrolled the same day … back in those days which was '51, I think. So uh, I think my parents just wanted me, to get me out of the house, I don't know. [laughs] I was, I'll never know. I forgot to ask my mother. But uh … that's the …
